brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Compact desk unit (small footprint, usable top)
requirements.evidence: 5 bases (3× full at 0,0,0 / 0,1,0 / 1,0,0 plus half-e at -1,0,0 and half-e at -1,0,1) with covers on top (cover:0,0,0;full;top, cover:0,1,0;full;top, cover:1,0,0;full;top, cover:-1,0,1;half-e;top), caps on open faces and joint bolts; meshClash clear.

Notch drawer frame installed at -1,1 level 0 (notch:0#-1,1#notch0, hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) filling the empty cell between -1,0,0 and 0,1,0. This is the system's drawer-in-notch implementation; provides pull-out storage for the desk. A half-base drawer (family drawer) requires a free cut face - the half-e at -1,0,0 is blocked by the adjacent full base at 0,0,0, so no drawer-family socket was offered, but drawer function is provided via the notch frame.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet, holding a small platform
requirements.evidence: Mount spike at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 (spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0) standing where pieces 0,0,0;full + 0,1,0;full + 1,0,0;full meet, variant mount with accessory platform-sm fitted via setSpikeAccessory.

finish.summary: Built compact 4+1 base desk with capped tops, a notch drawer frame at -1,1 providing drawer storage, and a mount spike with small platform at the triple-base corner (0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0). Mesh clear, open faces capped and joints locked.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
